statement: {R : Type u} → [inst : Ring R] → (I : Ideal R) → [I.IsTwoSided] → RingCon R

doc: The ring homomorphism from a ring `R` to a quotient ring `R/I`.
statement: {R : Type u} → [inst : Ring R] → (I : Ideal R) → [inst_1 : I.IsTwoSided] → R →+* R ⧸ I

doc:
Two `RingHom`s from the quotient by an ideal are equal if their
compositions with `Ideal.Quotient.mk'` are equal.

See note [partially-applied ext lemmas].
statement:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {I : Ideal R} {S : Type v} [inst_1 : I.IsTwoSided] [inst_2 : NonAssocSemiring S]
  ⦃f g : R ⧸ I →+* S⦄, f.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = g.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) → f = g

∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {I : Ideal R} {S : Type v} [inst_1 : I.IsTwoSided] [inst_2 : NonAssocSemiring S]
  {f g : R ⧸ I →+* S}, f = g ↔ f.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = g.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)

∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {I : Ideal R} {x y : R} [inst_1 : I.IsTwoSided],
  (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) x = (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) y ↔ x - y ∈ I

∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {I : Ideal R} [inst_1 : I.IsTwoSided] (x : R),
  Submodule.Quotient.mk x = (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) x
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {I : Ideal R} {a : R} [inst_1 : I.IsTwoSided], (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) a = 0 ↔ a ∈ I

∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {I : Ideal R} [inst_1 : I.IsTwoSided] (x y : R),
  (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) x = (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) y ↔ x - y ∈ I
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {I : Ideal R} [inst_1 : I.IsTwoSided] (x : R), (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) x = 1 ↔ x - 1 ∈ I

∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {I : Ideal R} [inst_1 : I.IsTwoSided] (x : R ⧸ I),
  (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) (Quotient.out x) = x
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {I : Ideal R} [inst_1 : I.IsTwoSided], Function.Surjective ⇑(Ideal.Quotient.mk I)

doc:
If `I` is an ideal of a commutative ring `R`, if `q : R → R/I` is the quotient map, and if
`s ⊆ R` is a subset, then `q⁻¹(q(s)) = ⋃ᵢ(i + s)`, the union running over all `i ∈ I`.
statement:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {I : Ideal R} [inst_1 : I.IsTwoSided] (s : Set R),
  ⇑(Ideal.Quotient.mk I) ⁻¹' ⇑(Ideal.Quotient.mk I) '' s = ⋃ x, (fun y => ↑x + y) '' s

doc:
Given a ring homomorphism `f : R →+* S` sending all elements of an ideal to zero,
lift it to the quotient by this ideal.
statement:
{R : Type u} →
  [inst : Ring R] →
    (I : Ideal R) →
      {S : Type v} → [inst_1 : I.IsTwoSided] → [inst_2 : Semiring S] → (f : R →+* S) → (∀ a ∈ I, f a = 0) → R ⧸ I →+* S

∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] (I : Ideal R) {a : R} {S : Type v} [inst_1 : I.IsTwoSided] [inst_2 : Semiring S]
  (f : R →+* S) (H : ∀ a ∈ I, f a = 0), (Ideal.Quotient.lift I f H) ((Ideal.Quotient.mk I) a) = f a

∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] (I : Ideal R) {S : Type v} [inst_1 : I.IsTwoSided] [inst_2 : Semiring S] (f : R →+* S)
  (H : ∀ a ∈ I, f a = 0), (Ideal.Quotient.lift I f H).comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = f

∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] (I : Ideal R) {S : Type v} [inst_1 : I.IsTwoSided] [inst_2 : Semiring S] {f : R →+* S}
  (H : ∀ a ∈ I, f a = 0), Function.Surjective ⇑f → Function.Surjective ⇑(Ideal.Quotient.lift I f H)

doc:
The ring homomorphism from the quotient by a smaller ideal to the quotient by a larger ideal.

This is the `Ideal.Quotient` version of `Quot.Factor`

When the two ideals are of the form `I^m` and `I^n` and `n ≤ m`,
please refer to the dedicated version `Ideal.Quotient.factorPow`.
statement:
{R : Type u} →
  [inst : Ring R] → {S T : Ideal R} → [inst_1 : S.IsTwoSided] → [inst_2 : T.IsTwoSided] → S ≤ T → R ⧸ S →+* R ⧸ T

∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {S T : Ideal R} [inst_1 : S.IsTwoSided] [inst_2 : T.IsTwoSided] (H : S ≤ T) (x : R),
  (Ideal.Quotient.factor H) ((Ideal.Quotient.mk S) x) = (Ideal.Quotient.mk T) x
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {S : Ideal R} [inst_1 : S.IsTwoSided], Ideal.Quotient.factor ⋯ = RingHom.id (R ⧸ S)

∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {S T : Ideal R} [inst_1 : S.IsTwoSided] [inst_2 : T.IsTwoSided] (H : S ≤ T),
  (Ideal.Quotient.factor H).comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk S) = Ideal.Quotient.mk T

∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {S T U : Ideal R} [inst_1 : S.IsTwoSided] [inst_2 : T.IsTwoSided] [inst_3 : U.IsTwoSided]
  (H1 : S ≤ T) (H2 : T ≤ U), (Ideal.Quotient.factor H2).comp (Ideal.Quotient.factor H1) = Ideal.Quotient.factor ⋯

∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {S T U : Ideal R} [inst_1 : S.IsTwoSided] [inst_2 : T.IsTwoSided] [inst_3 : U.IsTwoSided]
  (H1 : S ≤ T) (H2 : T ≤ U) (x : R ⧸ S),
  (Ideal.Quotient.factor H2) ((Ideal.Quotient.factor H1) x) = (Ideal.Quotient.factor ⋯) x

∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {S T : Ideal R} [inst_1 : S.IsTwoSided] [inst_2 : T.IsTwoSided] (H : S ≤ T),
  Function.Surjective ⇑(Ideal.Quotient.factor H)

doc:
Quotienting by equal ideals gives equivalent rings.

See also `Submodule.quotEquivOfEq` and `Ideal.quotientEquivAlgOfEq`.
statement:
{R : Type u} →
  [inst : Ring R] → {I J : Ideal R} → [inst_1 : I.IsTwoSided] → [inst_2 : J.IsTwoSided] → I = J → R ⧸ I ≃+* R ⧸ J

∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {I J : Ideal R} [inst_1 : I.IsTwoSided] [inst_2 : J.IsTwoSided] (h : I = J) (x : R),
  (Ideal.quotEquivOfEq h) ((Ideal.Quotient.mk I) x) = (Ideal.Quotient.mk J) x

∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {I J : Ideal R} [inst_1 : I.IsTwoSided] [inst_2 : J.IsTwoSided] (h : I = J),
  (Ideal.quotEquivOfEq h).symm = Ideal.quotEquivOfEq ⋯

∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Ring R] {I J : Ideal R} [inst_1 : I.IsTwoSided] [inst_2 : J.IsTwoSided] (h : I = J) (x : R ⧸ I),
  (Ideal.quotEquivOfEq h) x = (Ideal.Quotient.factor ⋯) x
